domain_label: DTC Plated-Jewelry Unit Economics — Per-Piece COGS Build-Up, Landed Cost & Working-Capital Reality
purpose: A method for assembling the honest per-piece cost of a plated fashion-jewelry item (base metal + gold/rhodium plating consumption from geometry x thickness x density + findings + labor + packaging, yield-adjusted) and carrying it through the correct jewelry HTS duty band (base-metal imitation 7117 ~11% vs precious-metal 7113 ~5% [FACT-HTSUS]) plus freight/fees to a landed COGS-to-stock, while exposing how plating thickness and base-metal choice move COGS and how MOQ + gold/rhodium inventory create a working-capital trap that can kill a per-unit-profitable venture, with every dollar tagged [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] and no price ever invented as measured.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all dollar figures are heuristic [ESTIMATE] bands with a stated method, never quoted invoices

the FTC Jewelry Guides 16 CFR Part 23 thickness/label definitions and the gold-density / troy-ounce constants are cited public [FACT]; the HTSUS jewelry duty bands (7117 base-metal imitation ~11%, 7113 precious-metal silver ~5% / gold ~5.5-5.8%) are cited [FACT-HTSUS] whose exact 10-digit suffix is [UNKNOWN] until composition and value are fixed

rhodium and gold input prices are live, volatile market references (spot XAU/USD, LBMA fix, PGM rhodium quotes) to be pulled at cost time, never hardened here [METHOD]; rhodium is priced far more volatilely than gold and can exceed it per gram

the piece is a costume/fashion (fashion-tier) plated item on a base-metal or sterling substrate, sold DTC; the specific SKU geometry, thickness spec, findings and packaging tier are inputs this KB accepts and stacks, not values it invents

any country-specific trade surcharge (e.g. Section-301 / reciprocal tariffs) layered on the MFN jewelry band is a separate volatile [UNKNOWN]-forward band to be re-confirmed per PO, not folded into the cited MFN rate

de-minimis duty-free entry for low-value parcels is treated as unavailable for the bulk-import operating model (repealed for all countries Aug 29 2025 [FACT-dated]); landed cost is modelled on a bulk Importer-of-Record entry, not ship-direct-per-order
exclusions: retail price-setting, keystone/perceived-value markup, contribution-margin-after-discount and price-band placement (that is kb2_pricing_and_margin; this KB stops at landed COGS-to-stock)
CAC, AOV, repeat/LTV, payback, break-even units and the go/no-go verdict (that is kb3_viability_cac_ltv)
the plating process physics, bath chemistry, adhesion/tarnish test methods and machine build (the supply-side materials/process specialists own those; this KB accepts their cost-relevant outputs)
consumer demand, category/finish share, demographics and the poll (the market and poll specialists own those)
asserting any specific supplier name, a measured factory cost, a live gold/rhodium price as fixed, or a market share as fact

competency_questions.question: What are the line items of a plated-jewelry piece's per-piece cost stack, and how do they roll up into a yield-adjusted COGS?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PIECE_COST_STACK_FRAME enumerates base metal + plating consumption + findings + labor + packaging as the BOM and YIELD_ADJUSTED_COGS rolls them into cost-per-GOOD-piece = summed cost / first-pass yield, all tagged [METHOD]/[ESTIMATE]

competency_questions.question: How is the gold/rhodium consumed per piece computed from the item's geometry, plating thickness and metal density?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GEOMETRY_SURFACE_AREA derives plated area (mm2) from the piece geometry and PLATING_MASS_MODEL computes mass = area x thickness x density (gold 19.32 g/cm3 [FACT], troy oz 31.1035 g) with thickness named the primary cost driver

competency_questions.question: What FTC thickness/label classes govern what a plated piece may legally be called, and where are their thresholds?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THICKNESS_TIER_FTC states 16 CFR 23 flash (<0.175 um), gold electroplate (>=0.175 um), heavy gold electroplate (2.5 um), vermeil (>=2.5 um >=10k gold over sterling) and that gold-filled is mechanically bonded not plated, all [FACT]

competency_questions.question: How do plating thickness and base-metal choice move the per-piece COGS?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THICKNESS_COGS_CURVE shows gold cost scaling roughly linearly with thickness (a 2.5 um heavy plate costing ~14x a 0.175 um flash in gold) while BASE_METAL_SUBSTRATE shows the base metal being a small direct cost but the lever that sets duty band and skin-safety

competency_questions.question: Why is rhodium plated over sterling silver, and what does that cost mechanism add to COGS?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RHODIUM_OVER_SILVER states rhodium is a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant platinum-group metal plated thinly (~0.05-0.25 um) over sterling/white gold to stop silver tarnish [FACT], and that its extreme, volatile PGM price makes even a thin layer a live cost input to pull, not guess

competency_questions.question: How is the precious-metal input priced honestly for the cost model without inventing a number?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRECIOUS_METAL_INPUT_PRICING states metal cost/piece = mass x ($/g incl. fabrication premium on salts/targets), pulled from live spot (XAU/USD, LBMA fix) and volatile rhodium PGM quotes [METHOD/FACT], never hardened

competency_questions.question: How do plating process losses and yield turn a nominal gold mass into a cost per good piece?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLATING_PROCESS_LOSSES names bath current efficiency, drag-out, target/anode utilization and rework as gold that is paid for but not on the product, and YIELD_ADJUSTED_COGS divides by first-pass yield to get cost-per-GOOD-piece

competency_questions.question: How is a plated piece classified for import and which jewelry HTS duty band applies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HTS_JEWELRY_CLASSIFICATION splits base-metal imitation jewelry (heading 7117) from precious-metal jewelry (heading 7113) by composition and JEWELRY_DUTY_BANDS states 7117 base-metal ~11% vs 7113 silver ~5% / gold ~5.5-5.8% [FACT-HTSUS] with the exact suffix and any country surcharge as [UNKNOWN]

competency_questions.question: How is landed COGS-to-stock computed from ex-works cost, duty, freight and fees for a small high-value parcel?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LANDED_COST_FORMULA stacks landed = ex-works x (1 + duty% + surcharge%) + freight + MPF/HMF/broker per piece, with FREIGHT_AND_FEES noting jewelry's high-value-low-weight makes air freight viable and per-piece freight small at bulk

competency_questions.question: How do MOQ and gold/rhodium inventory create the working-capital trap that can kill a per-unit-profitable venture?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MOQ_REALITY names per-style / per-plating-run / findings MOQs forcing units of cash out and WORKING_CAPITAL_TRAP states gold+inventory as the dominant working-capital line (DIO, cash-conversion cycle) so a per-unit-profitable brand can still die on cash timing [FACT/ESTIMATE]

competency_questions.question: How is the honesty discipline enforced so cost direction is trusted but no dollar is over-read as measured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONESTY_LEDGER separates the [FACT] anchors (FTC classes, gold density, HTS bands) from the [ESTIMATE] cost bands and the [UNKNOWN] live metal price / forward surcharge, and flags any single-point COGS as a band-centre illustration

competency_questions.question: What does this KB hand to the pricing and viability KBs, and what stays out of scope?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COGS_LANDED_HANDOFF delivers landed COGS-to-stock per piece with its thickness/base-metal sensitivity and working-capital conditions and stops before retail price, contribution and CAC/LTV

competency_questions.question: Why does the base-metal choice couple the cost stack to the duty band, and how is that resolved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASE_METAL_SUBSTRATE and JEWELRY_DUTY_BANDS show that a gold-plated-brass piece is base-metal imitation jewelry (7117 ~11%) while a rhodium-over-sterling piece is precious-metal jewelry (7113 ~5%), so the substrate is both a cost and a duty-band decision

glossary.definition: The bill-of-materials for one plated piece: base-metal substrate + plating metal consumed (gold/rhodium) + findings (posts, clasps, jump rings, chain, stones/CZ) + direct labor + packaging, summed then yield-adjusted to cost-per-GOOD-piece; the ex-works COGS this KB produces before duty and freight.

mass = plated surface area (cm2) x coating thickness (cm) x metal density; for gold density 19.32 g/cm3 [FACT], so a micron of gold over a known area converts to milligrams, and thickness is the primary lever on precious-metal cost; troy ounce = 31.1035 g is the pricing unit.

The US FTC Jewelry Guides plating definitions [FACT]: gold flash/wash below 0.175 um (cannot be called 'gold electroplate'); gold electroplate >=0.175 um; heavy gold electroplate 2.5 um; gold vermeil = gold of >=10k, >=2.5 um thick, electroplated over sterling silver; gold-filled is a thick mechanically bonded layer (>=1/20 by weight), NOT achievable by plating - a claim boundary.

Rhodium, a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant platinum-group metal, is electroplated in a very thin layer (~0.05-0.25 um) over sterling silver or white gold to give a bright white finish and stop the silver's sulfide tarnish [FACT]; its price is a volatile PGM quote that can exceed gold per gram, so even a thin layer is a live cost input, not a guess.

The core the plating sits on: base metals (brass, 316L stainless, copper, zinc/pewter alloys) are cheap and make the piece 'imitation jewellery' (HTS 7117); sterling silver 925 (92.5% Ag [FACT]) is dearer, is a precious metal, and makes even a plated piece 'precious-metal jewellery' (HTS 7113) - a cost, skin-safety and duty-band decision at once.

US import classification for jewelry [FACT-HTSUS]: imitation jewellery of base metal falls in heading 7117 (e.g. 7117.19 ~11% MFN); jewellery of precious metal falls in heading 7113 (silver 7113.11 ~5%, gold/other precious 7113.19 ~5.5-5.8% MFN); the exact 10-digit line and any country-specific surcharge are [UNKNOWN] until composition, value and origin are fixed.

cost-per-GOOD-piece = summed per-piece cost / first-pass yield; plating rework (strip-and-replate), adhesion/tarnish rejects and scrap mean paid-for gold and labor are spread over fewer sellable pieces, so a 90% yield inflates the good-piece cost by ~11%.

The true per-piece cost at the receiving door = ex-works COGS x (1 + duty% + surcharge%) + inbound freight + MPF/HMF + broker/entry fees, on a bulk Importer-of-Record entry; the whole output of this KB, read by the downstream pricing and viability KBs, never a retail price.

Minimum order quantities (per style from findings/casting vendors, per plating-run batch minimum, per findings pack) force units of cash out before any sale; combined with gold/rhodium inventory value this makes precious-metal + finished-goods stock the dominant working-capital line, so a brand profitable on every unit can still die on the months-long cash-conversion cycle.

The cost-down/quality-up spectrum: cheapest = flash gold over bright-nickel-over-brass, single layer, poly-bag packaging; premium = 2.5 um heavy gold or rhodium over sterling with a barrier/palladium interlayer, anti-tarnish topcoat and boxed packaging; the thickness and substrate levers move COGS far more than labor or packaging do.

nodes.definition: Establish the per-piece cost-stack frame every downstream number plugs into: the bill of materials for one plated fashion-jewelry piece is base-metal (or sterling) substrate + plating metal consumed (gold and/or rhodium) + findings (ear posts/backs, clasps, jump rings, chain, stones/CZ) + direct labor (plating line + assembly) + packaging, split into variable vs batch-amortized (setup) cost and rolled up per piece [METHOD]. This frame is deliberately a structure, not a number: it names the buckets, the variable/fixed split, and the batch-size amortization so that a change in one lever (thickness, substrate, findings) traces to a specific line. It excludes retail price, markup and CAC (downstream KBs) and the plating physics (materials specialist).

included: the BOM buckets: substrate, plating metal, findings, labor, packaging
variable-vs-batch-amortized cost split
per-piece roll-up as a structure not a value

pros.claim: A fixed cost-stack frame makes every later cost change traceable to a named line instead of a lump COGS
pros.example: moving from 0.5 um to 2.5 um plating changes only the plating-metal line, leaving findings and labor visibly unchanged

cons.claim: A frame alone quantifies nothing, so it can create a false sense of completeness before any line is filled
cons.example: an empty stack with all five buckets named still yields no COGS until geometry, thickness and prices are supplied

failure_modes: treating the frame as a finished cost model before the lines are populated with method-backed bands
folding retail markup or CAC into the cost stack and double-counting downstream
acceptance_tests: the five BOM buckets, the variable/batch split and the per-piece roll-up are stated as a [METHOD] structure with markup and CAC excluded
revisit_triggers: a new cost bucket appears (e.g. a duplex PVD topcoat step)
the downstream pricing KB changes what it expects handed off
the SKU form (earring vs chain) changes the dominant cost line

base.update_signal: the BOM structure or the downstream hand-off contract changes

nodes.definition: Derive the plated surface area per piece (mm2/cm2) from the item geometry, because area x thickness x density is the only honest route to gold mass. Method [METHOD/FACT]: for wire/chain, lateral surface area per unit length ~= pi x diameter x length; for a ring, area from band width x mean circumference (from ring-size); for studs/drops, sum the exposed faces; apply a coverage factor for clamp/rack shadow zones that do not receive full deposit. The output is a per-SKU plated-area number (a geometry calculation, honest and checkable), which feeds the mass model. It is not the finished area of any specific owner SKU until that SKU's dimensions are supplied.

included: lateral-area-per-length for wire/chain, band-area for rings, face-sum for studs/drops
coverage factor for shadowed zones
per-SKU plated area as a geometry output

pros.claim: Computing area from geometry keeps gold mass grounded in a checkable calculation rather than a vendor's claim
pros.example: a 1.2 mm chain's ~pi x 1.2 mm/mm lateral area gives a defensible per-cm area to plate

cons.claim: Real deposit is non-uniform (edges/high-current-density areas plate thicker), so a single area+nominal thickness under-captures local variation
cons.example: a ring's outer edge plates thicker than its inner band, so mass from mean area is an approximation

failure_modes: ignoring the coverage/shadow factor and over- or under-stating deposited area
using outer envelope area instead of true plated (wetted) area
acceptance_tests: a per-SKU plated area is derived from geometry (wire/chain lateral, ring band, stud faces) with a coverage factor, as a [METHOD] calculation
revisit_triggers: a new SKU form with different geometry is added
a plating-uniformity measurement shows the nominal-area approximation is off
the rack/clamp fixturing changes the shadowed area

base.update_signal: a new SKU geometry or a plating-uniformity measurement changes the area

nodes.definition: Convert plated area to precious-metal mass: mass = area (cm2) x thickness (cm) x density, with gold density 19.32 g/cm3 [FACT] and rhodium ~12.4 g/cm3 [FACT]; troy ounce = 31.1035 g is the pricing unit. Thickness is the primary cost driver [FACT]: at fixed area, a 2.5 um heavy plate consumes ~14x the gold of a 0.175 um flash, so the micron spec, more than any other single lever, sets the metal cost. A worked illustration [ESTIMATE, method-transparent]: ~1 cm2 at 1 um gold ~= 0.00193 g ~= 1.93 mg; at 2.5 um ~= 4.8 mg. This model outputs milligrams-per-piece and grams-per-1000-pieces; the dollar value comes only when a live price is applied downstream.

included: mass = area x thickness x density with gold 19.32 / rhodium ~12.4 g/cm3 [FACT]
thickness as the primary cost driver
mg-per-piece and g-per-1000-piece outputs
excluded: the FTC label thresholds on thickness (THICKNESS_TIER_FTC)
the $/g price applied to the mass (PRECIOUS_METAL_INPUT_PRICING)

pros.claim: A physics identity (area x thickness x density) ties gold mass to two measurable inputs and one constant, making the metal cost auditable
pros.example: showing 1 cm2 at 2.5 um = ~4.8 mg lets a reviewer recompute the gold line independently

cons.claim: Nominal thickness understates true consumption because deposit thickness is non-uniform and drag-out/overspray waste gold beyond what lands on the piece
cons.example: a nominal 2.5 um spec may draw >2.5 um of gold from the bath once edge build-up and losses are counted

failure_modes: applying the gold density to a rhodium layer (or vice versa) and mis-sizing the mass
using nominal thickness as delivered mass and ignoring process losses handled downstream
acceptance_tests: mass = area x thickness x density is stated with gold 19.32 / rhodium ~12.4 g/cm3 and troy oz 31.1035 g [FACT], thickness named the primary driver, and a worked mg-per-cm2 illustration
revisit_triggers: the thickness spec of a SKU changes
a measured mass-balance reconciliation shows nominal mass off
a switch between gold and rhodium (or a duplex stack) changes which density applies

base.update_signal: a thickness spec, a density (metal switch), or a mass-balance reconciliation changes

nodes.definition: Fix the FTC Jewelry Guides 16 CFR Part 23 thickness/label classes that govern what a plated piece may legally be called and thereby bound the cheapest honest stack [FACT]: gold flash/wash below 0.175 um cannot be called 'gold electroplate'; gold electroplate requires gold of at least 10 karat AND >=0.175 um; heavy gold electroplate requires >=10k AND >=2.5 um; gold vermeil requires gold of at least 10 karat, at least 2.5 um thick, electroplated over a sterling-silver base; gold-filled is a thick, mechanically bonded layer (>=1/20 by weight) and is NOT achievable by electroplating - a hard claim boundary. These thresholds mean the label the piece can carry, and the marketing claim, are a function of the plating thickness the cost model chose.

included: the 16 CFR 23 flash/electroplate/heavy/vermeil thresholds [FACT]
gold-filled as mechanically bonded, not plated
label class as a function of chosen thickness

pros.claim: Anchoring the label thresholds keeps the cheapest stack legal and prevents an overstated 'gold electroplate' or 'vermeil' claim
pros.example: a 0.1 um flash saving gold cannot be sold as 'gold electroplate' - the 0.175 um floor forces an honest label

cons.claim: The FTC classes bound the claim but not the wear life, so a piece can be legally labelled yet still wear poorly at the minimum thickness
cons.example: a just-legal 0.175 um electroplate meets the label but may rub through quickly on a high-wear ring

failure_modes: labelling a sub-0.175 um flash as 'gold electroplate' in violation of 16 CFR 23
claiming 'vermeil' on a gold-over-brass piece when vermeil requires a sterling-silver base
acceptance_tests: the flash (<0.175 um), electroplate (>=0.175 um), heavy (2.5 um) and vermeil (>=10k, >=2.5 um, over sterling) thresholds and the gold-filled-not-plated boundary are stated as [FACT]
revisit_triggers: the FTC Jewelry Guides are amended
a SKU's marketing claim changes and needs a thickness/label re-check
a vermeil claim is proposed on a non-sterling substrate

base.update_signal: an FTC guide amendment or a label/claim change occurs

nodes.definition: Model the substrate decision, which is simultaneously a cost, a skin-safety and a duty-band lever. Base metals - brass, 316L stainless, copper, zinc/pewter alloys - are cheap (commodity $/kg) and make the finished piece 'imitation jewellery'; sterling silver 925 (92.5% Ag [FACT]) is much dearer, is itself a precious metal, and makes even a plated piece 'precious-metal jewellery'. Skin-safety couples in: nickel-bearing bases must meet the EN1811 nickel-release limit (0.5 ug/cm2/week [FACT]) for prolonged skin contact, favouring a nickel-free brass or a barrier layer for 18-25 skin-contact wear. The direct substrate cost is usually a small line versus gold, but the choice sets the HTS heading (7117 vs 7113) downstream, so it is a bigger economic decision than its BOM line suggests.

included: base-metal vs sterling substrate cost
EN1811 nickel-release skin-safety [FACT]
the substrate as the lever that sets the HTS heading

pros.claim: Treating the substrate as a duty-and-safety lever, not just a cheap BOM line, surfaces its outsized economic weight
pros.example: switching a plated piece from brass to sterling roughly halves the import duty band (11% to ~5%) even though the metal costs more

cons.claim: Sterling's higher metal cost and tarnish tendency can outweigh the duty saving for a low-value costume piece
cons.example: a $2 costume earring gains little from a sterling core whose silver cost dwarfs the duty difference

failure_modes: choosing a nickel-bearing base for skin-contact wear without an EN1811 check or barrier layer
treating the substrate as a trivial cost line and missing its duty-band consequence
acceptance_tests: base-metal vs sterling substrate cost, the EN1811 nickel-release limit [FACT], and the substrate-sets-HTS-heading coupling are all stated
revisit_triggers: a SKU switches substrate (brass<->sterling)
the nickel-release compliance requirement for the target market changes
the gold/silver price ratio shifts the substrate-vs-plating cost balance

base.update_signal: a substrate switch, a nickel-compliance change, or a metal-price-ratio shift occurs

nodes.definition: Carry the correct rhodium science and its cost mechanism, sharpening the owner's roughly-right intuition. Rhodium is a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant platinum-group metal; it is electroplated in a very thin layer (~0.05-0.25 um typical) over sterling silver or white gold to give a bright white finish and, crucially, to stop the underlying silver from tarnishing (silver reacts with sulfur to form dark silver sulfide; the inert rhodium barrier prevents that reaction) [FACT]. Economically: because the layer is thin, the rhodium MASS per piece is small, but rhodium is a thinly-traded PGM whose price is extremely volatile and has at times exceeded gold per gram, so even a thin layer is a live, must-pull cost input, never a guessed constant. Rhodium also wears/needs re-plating over time - a warranty/re-plate reserve consideration, not a per-piece COGS add.

included: rhodium as a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant PGM over sterling/white gold [FACT]
the thin ~0.05-0.25 um layer and small but price-volatile mass
the tarnish-prevention mechanism (barrier over sulfide-forming silver)

pros.claim: Stating the correct rhodium science lets the cost model treat it as a thin-but-volatile input rather than under- or over-costing it
pros.example: recognising a ~0.1 um rhodium layer as small mass but volatile price flags it as a must-pull, not a fixed line

cons.claim: Rhodium's price volatility makes its cost line the least stable in the stack even though its mass is tiny
cons.example: a rhodium price spike can move the rhodium line several-fold week to week while gold barely moves

failure_modes: hardening a stale rhodium price into the cost model despite its extreme volatility
describing rhodium as merely 'making silver shiny' and missing that it is the tarnish barrier and a wear/re-plate item
acceptance_tests: rhodium as a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant PGM plated thinly over sterling/white gold, the sulfide-tarnish-barrier mechanism [FACT], and the small-mass-but-volatile-price cost consequence are stated
revisit_triggers: the rhodium PGM price moves materially
a SKU adds or drops a rhodium finish
a re-plate/warranty policy is set that touches the rhodium wear question

base.update_signal: a rhodium price move or a finish/warranty change occurs

nodes.definition: Define how the precious-metal input is priced honestly: metal cost per piece = mass-per-piece (from PLATING_MASS_MODEL) x $/g, where $/g is the live spot price plus a fabrication premium, never a hardened guess [METHOD/FACT]. Gold: pull spot XAU/USD or the LBMA gold price fix at cost time; the plating input (potassium gold cyanide or sulfite gold salt, or a sputter target) carries a fabrication premium over spot because the salt/target costs more than grain. Rhodium: pull a current PGM rhodium quote (thin market, volatile). The KB supplies the method and the constants (troy oz, karat weight fraction of the deposit alloy), not a fixed price; any illustrative $/g is tagged [ESTIMATE, pull-live] so the direction of the gold line is trusted while its level stays a live quote.

included: metal cost = mass x ($/g incl. fabrication premium) as a [METHOD]
spot/LBMA gold and volatile rhodium quotes as the live source
karat weight-fraction of the deposit alloy

pros.claim: Pricing metal as mass x live-$/g keeps the gold line honest and re-pullable instead of a stale invented number
pros.example: the same mass model re-priced at a new spot instantly updates the gold line without touching the geometry

cons.claim: A live-price method means the metal line can never be quoted as a fixed cost, which frustrates a demand for one COGS number
cons.example: a stakeholder wanting a single gold cost must accept a spot-dependent band

failure_modes: pricing off spot grain and ignoring the fabrication premium on salts/targets, understating the metal line
hardening a single day's gold/rhodium price into the model as if it were fixed
acceptance_tests: metal cost = mass x ($/g incl. fabrication premium), pulled from live spot/LBMA gold and volatile rhodium quotes, with any illustrative $/g tagged [ESTIMATE, pull-live] is stated
revisit_triggers: the gold or rhodium price moves materially
the plating input form changes (salt vs target, karat)
the fabrication premium quoted by the chemistry house changes

base.update_signal: the gold/rhodium price, input form, or fabrication premium changes

nodes.definition: Cost the non-plating physical components: findings (ear posts and backs, clasps, jump rings, chain by the metre, pin stems), and any set stones (cubic zirconia, glass, resin) or beads, as sourced parts with their own per-piece cost and MOQ [METHOD]. For many small pieces (studs, thin chains) findings are a modest line; for assembled pieces (a necklace with clasp + chain + pendant + jump rings) findings can rival or exceed the plating-metal cost. These are bought-in components priced from supplier quotes (not invented here) and carry their own minimum-buy quantities that feed the working-capital picture. The KB names the buckets and the method to price them; the actual per-part cost is a [UNKNOWN] until a supplier quotes it.

included: findings (posts/backs/clasps/jump rings/chain) and set stones as bought-in per-piece parts
findings can rival plating cost on assembled pieces
component MOQ feeding working capital

pros.claim: Costing findings as their own line stops assembled pieces from being under-costed on plating alone
pros.example: a necklace's clasp + chain + jump rings can exceed its plated-pendant gold cost, which a plating-only model would miss

cons.claim: Findings cost is a per-supplier [UNKNOWN] until quoted, so the line stays a placeholder band early on
cons.example: a clasp's cost varies widely by material and volume, so an early estimate is soft

failure_modes: costing only the plated body and omitting findings on assembled SKUs
inventing a per-part findings price instead of pricing from a supplier quote
acceptance_tests: findings (posts/backs/clasps/jump rings/chain) and stones are stated as bought-in per-piece parts priced [METHOD] from supplier quotes, with findings able to rival plating cost on assembled pieces
revisit_triggers: a findings supplier quote lands
a SKU's construction changes (more/fewer components)
a findings material switch (e.g. to sterling posts for skin-safety) changes the line

base.update_signal: a findings quote or a SKU construction change occurs

nodes.definition: Account for the gold that is paid for but does not end up as sellable coating, because nominal mass understates real consumption [FACT/METHOD]. Electroplating route: cathode current efficiency below 100%, drag-out loss on racks/spools withdrawn from the bath, plate-out on tank hardware, and replenisher dosing all consume gold beyond what lands on the piece; a save-rinse and electrowinning recover some. Sputtering route: magnetron target utilization is limited (planar racetrack erosion), and chamber-wall/shield overspray captures gold not deposited on product. The KB tracks a gold-in / gold-on-product / gold-recoverable balance and expresses the loss as a utilization factor that inflates the effective mass (hence cost) per piece. Scrap gold has recovery value (toll refining) that credits back against the loss.

included: bath current efficiency, drag-out, plate-out losses; sputter target utilization and overspray
gold-in/on-product/recoverable balance and a utilization factor
scrap recovery credit

pros.claim: Inflating nominal mass by a utilization factor prevents systematically under-costing the gold line
pros.example: at 60% effective utilization, the gold cost per piece is ~1.67x the nominal-mass cost

cons.claim: The utilization factor is process- and scale-dependent, so it is an [ESTIMATE] until a real mass balance is run at the owner's line
cons.example: a small hand-plating operation may waste far more gold per piece than a mature line, widening the band

failure_modes: using nominal deposited mass as gold purchased and understating the metal line
ignoring the scrap-recovery credit and overstating the net loss
acceptance_tests: bath current efficiency, drag-out and target-utilization losses, a gold-in/on-product/recoverable balance, a utilization factor inflating effective mass, and the scrap-recovery credit are stated
revisit_triggers: a measured gold mass-balance at the owner's line lands
a route switch (electroplate vs sputter) changes the utilization profile

nodes.definition: Model inbound freight and federal fees for jewelry, whose high-value-low-weight profile differs from bulky goods [FACT/METHOD]. conflict_axes.name: per_unit_profit_vs_working_capital_cycle
conflict_axes.description: A piece can be profitable per landed unit yet the venture die on the months-long MOQ-driven, gold-heavy cash-conversion cycle, so per-unit viability is necessary not sufficient.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fund the MOQ + gold inventory cash cycle before the first bulk buy; per-unit profit is necessary not sufficient

conflict_axes.name: live_metal_price_vs_single_cogs_number
conflict_axes.description: Stakeholders want one COGS per piece while the gold/rhodium price is live and volatile, so the metal line and the COGS can only be an honest band.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: price metal as mass x live-$/g and label any single COGS a band-centre illustration robust in direction, soft in level

conflict_axes.name: small_lot_premium_vs_tied_up_capital
conflict_axes.description: Small orders pay a per-unit setup premium while large orders trade that premium for capital tied up in MOQ-sized gold-heavy inventory.
poles: large lots to cut per-unit cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: size the run to the launch cash the venture can fund, not the lowest per-unit price; the cheapest per-unit MOQ can be the cash-fatal one

conflict_axes.name: cost_down_by_value_engineering_vs_by_degrading
conflict_axes.description: Lowering price can be done by value-engineering the stack (tune thickness, substrate, barrier layer, batch size) or by crudely degrading quality (sub-floor flash, no barrier), which erases perceived and real quality.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cut cost by tuning the thickness/substrate/batch levers to the quality floor, never below it; degrading below the wear/label floor is not a cost saving

conflict_axes.name: nominal_mass_vs_process_loss_true_gold
conflict_axes.description: Nominal deposited mass understates the gold actually purchased because bath/drag-out/target losses consume gold that never lands on the piece.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: inflate nominal mass by a measured utilization factor and credit scrap recovery; nominal-only understates the metal line

conflict_axes.name: ex_works_stack_vs_border_as_cogs_driver
conflict_axes.description: Unlike high-duty apparel, jewelry's modest ~5-11% duty and small freight mean the ex-works gold/findings/yield stack, not the border, drives COGS - a temptation to over-focus on tariffs.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the ex-works stack as the main COGS driver and the border as a modest uplift, unless a large country surcharge inverts that

conflict_axes.name: known_mfn_band_vs_unknown_country_surcharge
conflict_axes.description: The MFN jewelry duty bands are firm [FACT] while any origin-specific surcharge is volatile and [UNKNOWN] forward, so an all-in duty can be over- or under-stated.
poles: anchor on the firm MFN band
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the MFN band as the citeable anchor and carry any country surcharge as a separate [UNKNOWN]-forward band re-confirmed per PO and origin

edge_cases.description: A cost-down pushes plating below the 0.175 um FTC floor, so the piece can no longer be legally called 'gold electroplate' and rubs through quickly
edge_cases.trigger: a gold-saving thickness cut drops below the FTC electroplate floor or the wear minimum
edge_cases.mitigation: hold thickness at or above the FTC 0.175 um floor and the wear-tested minimum; label the piece honestly for the thickness actually plated

edge_cases.description: A gold-plated-brass costume piece is classified as precious-metal jewellery (7113) and under-declares duty, or a sterling piece is mis-declared as 7117
edge_cases.trigger: a piece is classified by its plating metal instead of its base-metal/precious substrate
edge_cases.mitigation: classify by substrate composition (7117 base-metal vs 7113 precious) and confirm the 10-digit line before entry

edge_cases.description: A rhodium price spike multiplies the rhodium line week-to-week while a stale price sits hardened in the cost model
edge_cases.trigger: the volatile PGM rhodium price moves materially after the model priced it
edge_cases.mitigation: pull a live rhodium quote at cost time and re-price; never harden a rhodium $/g

edge_cases.description: A 6-SKU launch is costed as per-piece COGS x 6 and the MOQ-forced run-sized cash commitment is missed, stranding the venture on cash
edge_cases.trigger: launch cash is planned on unit COGS without the per-style MOQ and plating batch minimum
edge_cases.mitigation: size launch cash on run-sized MOQ x SKUs plus gold inventory, and fund the cash cycle before the first buy

edge_cases.description: The metal line is priced off spot grain and ignores the fabrication premium on salts/targets, understating the gold cost
edge_cases.trigger: the model prices gold at spot without the salt/target fabrication premium
edge_cases.mitigation: price the actual plating input (salt/target) at spot + fabrication premium, not raw grain

edge_cases.description: Nominal deposited mass is used as gold purchased, ignoring bath/drag-out/target losses, so the metal line is understated
edge_cases.trigger: the cost model omits the process-loss utilization factor
edge_cases.mitigation: inflate nominal mass by a measured utilization factor and credit scrap recovery

edge_cases.description: A single band-centre COGS figure is quoted to a stakeholder as a measured per-piece cost despite the live-price and yield uncertainty
edge_cases.trigger: a single-point COGS is read as a fact rather than a band-centre illustration
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the band and label any point a band-centre illustration robust in direction, soft in level

edge_cases.description: Findings cost is omitted on an assembled necklace and only the plated pendant is costed, materially under-costing the piece
edge_cases.trigger: an assembled SKU is costed on plating metal alone
edge_cases.mitigation: cost every finding (chain, clasp, jump rings) as its own line; on assembled pieces findings can rival the gold cost

edge_cases.description: A nickel-bearing base metal is used for a skin-contact piece without an EN1811 check or barrier layer, risking a nickel-release non-compliance
edge_cases.trigger: a skin-contact SKU uses a nickel-bearing substrate without a nickel-release control
edge_cases.mitigation: use a nickel-free base or a barrier layer and verify against the EN1811 0.5 ug/cm2/week limit

edge_cases.description: A ship-direct-per-order plan is modelled as if low-value parcels still entered duty-free after the Aug 29 2025 de-minimis repeal
edge_cases.trigger: the import model assumes duty-free low-value parcels post-repeal
edge_cases.mitigation: model a bulk Importer-of-Record entry; every parcel is now dutiable and per-entry fees punish per-order

edge_cases.description: A large origin-specific trade surcharge lands and dwarfs the modest ~5-11% MFN duty gap the model planned on
edge_cases.trigger: a Section-301/reciprocal tariff by origin is announced during the buy window
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the country surcharge as a separate [UNKNOWN]-forward band, re-confirm per PO and origin, and stress-test the landed COGS

workflow.action: Lay out the per-piece cost-stack frame
workflow.description: Name the BOM buckets (substrate, plating metal, findings, labor, packaging) and the variable/batch-amortized split
workflow.gate: the five buckets and the variable/fixed split are stated as a [METHOD] structure

workflow.action: Compute plated area and precious-metal mass
workflow.description: Derive plated area from geometry and convert to gold/rhodium mass via area x thickness x density
workflow.gate: a per-SKU plated area and mass = area x thickness x density with gold 19.32 g/cm3 are stated

workflow.description: State the 16 CFR 23 flash/electroplate/heavy/vermeil thresholds and the gold-filled boundary
workflow.gate: the FTC thresholds and the gold-filled-not-plated boundary are stated as [FACT]

workflow.action: Decide the substrate and rhodium finish
workflow.description: Choose base-metal vs sterling with skin-safety, and state the rhodium-over-silver science and cost mechanism
workflow.gate: the substrate cost/skin/duty coupling and the rhodium PGM tarnish-barrier science are stated

workflow.action: Price the metal and account for process losses
workflow.description: Apply live $/g + fabrication premium to loss-inflated mass to get effective gold cost per piece
workflow.gate: metal cost = loss-inflated mass x live $/g (incl. premium) with a utilization factor and scrap credit is stated

workflow.action: Roll up the yield-adjusted ex-works COGS
workflow.description: Sum all buckets and divide by first-pass yield for cost-per-good-piece
workflow.gate: the summed cost and cost-per-good-piece = nominal / first-pass yield are stated as a band

workflow.description: Show thickness driving the gold line ~linearly and the base-metal duty-band flip; give the cheapest-vs-premium stack map
workflow.gate: the thickness (~14x flash-to-heavy) and substrate levers and the stack map are stated

workflow.action: Classify for import and set the duty band
workflow.description: Classify 7117 vs 7113 by substrate and state the ~11% vs ~5% MFN bands plus the [UNKNOWN] surcharge
workflow.gate: the 7117/7113 split, the ~11% vs ~5-5.8% MFN bands, and the separate country surcharge are stated

workflow.description: Recompute landed = ex-works x (1 + duty% + surcharge%) + freight + fees per piece
workflow.gate: the landed stack is stated, recomputes the base-metal vs sterling cases, and names the ex-works stack as the main driver

workflow.action: Size MOQ and the working-capital trap
workflow.description: Name the run-sized MOQ cash commitment and the gold-heavy cash-conversion cycle as a fund-first condition
workflow.gate: the MOQ cash commitment and the profitable-per-unit-yet-die-on-cash trap are stated as a condition not a COGS add

workflow.description: Separate [FACT] anchors from [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] soft inputs and flag any single-point COGS
workflow.gate: the [FACT] anchors, the soft inputs, and the band-centre-illustration flag are enumerated

workflow.description: Deliver the landed COGS band with sensitivity and the binding conditions, stopping before price/CAC
workflow.gate: the landed band, the sensitivity, the clean pre-pricing boundary and the four binding conditions are stated

dominance_rules.rule: The FTC/wear thickness floor dominates a gold-saving thickness cut
dominance_rules.rationale: plating below the 0.175 um FTC floor or the wear minimum voids the legal label and generates returns that erase the saving
dominance_rules.trigger: a cost-down proposes thinning plating below the FTC/wear floor
dominance_rules.action: hold thickness at or above the floor and label honestly for the thickness plated

dominance_rules.rule: Substrate composition dominates plating metal in HTS classification
dominance_rules.rationale: the piece is classified by what it is made of (7117 base-metal vs 7113 precious), not what it is plated with
dominance_rules.trigger: a piece is being classified by its coating metal
dominance_rules.action: classify by base-metal/precious substrate and confirm the 10-digit line before entry

dominance_rules.rule: Live metal price dominates any hardened gold/rhodium figure
dominance_rules.rationale: gold and especially rhodium are volatile, so a hardened price mis-states the metal line
dominance_rules.trigger: a cost model carries a fixed gold/rhodium $/g
dominance_rules.action: price mass x live spot + fabrication premium and re-pull at cost time

dominance_rules.rule: Loss-inflated purchased gold dominates nominal deposited mass
dominance_rules.rationale: bath/drag-out/target losses mean more gold is bought than lands on the piece
dominance_rules.trigger: the metal line uses nominal deposited mass as gold purchased
dominance_rules.action: inflate by a measured utilization factor and credit scrap recovery

dominance_rules.rationale: rework and rejects spread paid-for gold and labor over fewer sellable pieces
dominance_rules.trigger: a COGS is quoted from the nominal BOM without yield
dominance_rules.action: divide nominal cost by first-pass yield

dominance_rules.rule: Working-capital survival dominates per-unit landed profit
dominance_rules.rationale: a per-unit-profitable brand can still die on the MOQ-driven gold-heavy cash cycle
dominance_rules.trigger: a go decision rests on per-unit landed margin alone
dominance_rules.action: require the MOQ + gold inventory cash cycle to be funded before the first bulk buy

dominance_rules.rule: The ex-works stack dominates the border as the jewelry COGS driver
dominance_rules.rationale: modest ~5-11% duty and small freight make gold/findings/yield the main cost, unlike high-duty apparel
dominance_rules.trigger: a cost analysis over-focuses on tariffs
dominance_rules.action: drive COGS work from the ex-works stack and treat the border as a modest uplift unless a large surcharge inverts it

dominance_rules.rule: The firm MFN band dominates, and the country surcharge is carried separately
dominance_rules.rationale: the MFN band is cited [FACT] while any origin surcharge is volatile [UNKNOWN] forward
dominance_rules.trigger: an all-in duty folds a guessed surcharge into the MFN rate
dominance_rules.action: quote the MFN band as the anchor and carry the surcharge as a separate [UNKNOWN] band re-confirmed per PO/origin

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute gold mass from geometry x thickness x density before pricing any metal line
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a vendor-claimed or guessed gold cost that must be re-derived once the real area/thickness is known

anti_rework_rules.rule: Price metal as mass x live $/g + fabrication premium from the outset, never a hardened figure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole cost model built on a stale gold/rhodium price that a market move invalidates

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the process-loss utilization factor and first-pass yield in the same roll-up
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a nominal COGS that understates gold and rejects and must be corrected up later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Classify by substrate (7117 vs 7113) and confirm the duty band before landing any piece
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mis-declared entry and a landed-cost re-work after a classification correction

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold thickness at the FTC/wear floor when value-engineering cost down
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a sub-floor flash that voids the label or wears through and generates returns, undoing the saving

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size launch cash on run-sized MOQ x SKUs plus gold inventory, not unit COGS x 6
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a launch that is per-unit profitable but stalls on unfunded MOQ-driven working capital

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry the country surcharge as a separate [UNKNOWN]-forward band from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an all-in duty hardened on a guessed surcharge that a tariff action invalidates

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every single-point COGS a band-centre illustration when first produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a band-centre point circulating as a measured cost and having to be retracted

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live gold or rhodium price is pulled at cost time
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the metal line and re-roll the ex-works and landed COGS bands

iteration_protocol.trigger: the first-pass yield or the process-loss utilization factor is measured at the owner's line
iteration_protocol.action: update the loss factor and yield division and re-roll the COGS

iteration_protocol.trigger: a supplier quotes findings, plating batch minimum or MOQ
iteration_protocol.action: replace the findings [UNKNOWN] and re-size the MOQ working-capital commitment

iteration_protocol.trigger: a SKU's thickness spec or substrate changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the mass model, the FTC label check, the thickness/substrate sensitivity and the HTS classification

iteration_protocol.trigger: a USITC MFN rate change or a country-specific trade surcharge is announced or sunsets
iteration_protocol.action: update the duty band and surcharge and re-run the landed stack

iteration_protocol.trigger: a CBP classification ruling or a de-minimis/MPF fee change lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-confirm the 7117/7113 classification and the freight/fee lines

iteration_protocol.trigger: the DIO / cash-conversion cycle or the gold-inventory exposure is measured for the venture
iteration_protocol.action: quantify the working-capital trap and update the hand-off conditions

priority_rationale: The cost-stack frame, geometry, mass model, FTC thickness classes and substrate come first because every metal and cost number depends on the plated area, the thickness spec, the density constant and the base-metal choice; the rhodium science, metal pricing, findings, process losses, labor and packaging next, because they populate the individual BOM lines; the yield-adjusted roll-up and the thickness/substrate sensitivity then assemble and stress the ex-works COGS; the HTS classification, duty bands, freight/fees and landed formula convert ex-works into landed COGS-to-stock; and the MOQ, working-capital, honesty and hand-off nodes come last because they compose the cash-cycle reality, the tagging discipline and the clean boundary before the pricing and viability KBs.
